name: Bay Area Geography
description: Get oriented as a Bay Area newcomer: the bay-centered mental map, the regions around it, the bridges that link them, the transit systems that cross them, and the East Bay essentials for daily life.

fields.front: Standing anywhere in San Francisco, the Pacific Ocean lies in which direction?
fields.extra: The bay is on the opposite side, to the east. Same trick as Chicago's lake, mirrored: water on the west edge means you're facing the ocean, not the bay.

fields.front: San Francisco sits on what kind of landform?
fields.back: The northern tip of a peninsula.
fields.extra: Pacific to the west, bay to the east, the Golden Gate strait to the north. The city is boxed in by water on three sides, which is why it stays only 7x7 miles.

fields.front: Walking uphill in Berkeley means you are heading in which direction?
fields.extra: Downhill is always west toward the bay: the East Bay's version of the ocean-is-west trick. Locals call the low bayside neighborhoods "the flats" and everything up top "the hills".

fields.front: Berkeley and Oakland are in which Bay Area region?
fields.extra: Everything across the bay to the east of San Francisco: Oakland, Berkeley, and their surrounding cities.

fields.front: Berkeley and Oakland are in which county?
fields.extra: Counties matter here: they run elections, courts, and public health. County siblings: cross the hills eastward and you are in Contra Costa County.

fields.front: Driving east from Berkeley or Oakland "through the tunnel" puts you in which county?
fields.extra: The Caldecott Tunnel carries Highway 24 through the hills to Orinda, Lafayette, and Walnut Creek. "Through the tunnel" is the local shorthand for that whole hotter, suburban side.

fields.front: Which small city sits on the bay shore between Berkeley and Oakland?
fields.extra: The East Bay's big-box shopping stop (IKEA, Bay Street) and home of Pixar. You pass it every time you head for the Bay Bridge.

fields.front: Marin County belongs to which Bay Area region?
fields.extra: Cross the Golden Gate Bridge and you are in Marin; keep going north for Napa and Sonoma wine country.

fields.front: The stretch of suburbs running south from San Francisco along the bay is called what?
fields.extra: San Mateo, Redwood City, Palo Alto. Locals mean these suburbs, not San Francisco itself, even though the city sits on the same landmass.

fields.front: "Silicon Valley" mostly overlaps with which Bay Area region?
fields.extra: The Santa Clara Valley at the bay's southern end: San Jose, Santa Clara, Cupertino, Mountain View.

fields.front: Which Bay Area city has the largest population?
fields.extra: Roughly a million people, more than San Francisco. It anchors the South Bay.

fields.front: Which bridge carries traffic between San Francisco and Oakland?
fields.extra: The commuter workhorse, carrying I-80. Tourists photograph the Golden Gate; commuters sit in traffic on the Bay Bridge.

fields.front: The Golden Gate Bridge connects San Francisco to which county?
fields.extra: It is the gateway north, not east: going to Oakland means the Bay Bridge, never the Golden Gate.

fields.front: Apart from the bridge named after it, what is "the Golden Gate" itself?
fields.back: The strait where the bay opens into the Pacific.
fields.extra: The bay's only outlet to the ocean. The strait was named before the bridge existed, and the fog pours in through it.

fields.front: Which bridge takes you from the East Bay to Marin without going through San Francisco?
fields.extra: Carries I-580 across the bay's northern arm. From Berkeley it is the direct route to Marin's trails and the coast.

fields.front: Which island sits in the middle of the bay, halfway along the Bay Bridge?
fields.extra: Man-made for the 1939 world's fair. It is attached to the natural Yerba Buena Island, which the bridge actually tunnels through.

fields.front: Which bay island is the famous former federal prison?
fields.extra: "The Rock", sitting alone off the San Francisco waterfront, prison until 1963. Island siblings: Treasure Island carries the Bay Bridge; Angel Island is the big green park.

fields.front: What is the largest natural island in San Francisco Bay?
fields.extra: A ferry-reached state park off Tiburon, once the "Ellis Island of the West" immigration station. Big and green, unlike barren little Alcatraz.

fields.front: What is BART?
fields.back: The Bay Area's regional metro rail system (Bay Area Rapid Transit).
fields.extra: Links San Francisco, the East Bay, and SFO airport. Think regional rail between cities, not a city subway.

fields.front: How does BART cross the bay between San Francisco and Oakland?
fields.back: Through an underwater tunnel, the Transbay Tube.
fields.extra: Not over a bridge: the tube sits on the bay floor, which is why trains get loud on that stretch.

fields.front: Which train line runs down the Peninsula from San Francisco to San Jose?
fields.extra: BART barely touches the Peninsula (only as far as SFO/Millbrae); Caltrain is how you rail south.

fields.front: What is Muni?
fields.back: San Francisco's own city transit system (buses, streetcars, cable cars).
fields.extra: Muni moves you within SF; BART moves you between cities. The two share some downtown stations.

fields.front: Which agency runs the East Bay's local buses?
fields.extra: Transit siblings: Muni is SF's system, BART is the regional rail, AC Transit is your Berkeley/Oakland bus. Its transbay lines also cross the Bay Bridge into SF.

fields.front: Which major airport is in the East Bay?
fields.extra: From Berkeley usually the easy airport; SFO means crossing the bay. Third sibling: SJC, down in San Jose.

fields.front: I-80 East out of the Bay Area is the road to which state capital?
fields.extra: And beyond it, the Sierra and Lake Tahoe: the classic winter weekend drive. The same I-80 westbound is Berkeley's freeway to the Bay Bridge.

fields.front: When Bay Area locals say "the City", which city do they mean?
fields.extra: Even people in San Jose, a bigger city, say it. "SF" is fine too; "San Fran" marks you as a newcomer.

fields.front: When East Bay locals say "the Town", which city do they mean?
fields.extra: The proud counterpart to "the City" for San Francisco; you'll see "Town" on Oakland merch everywhere.

fields.front: Which side of San Francisco gets most of the fog?
fields.back: The west side, facing the Pacific.
fields.extra: Fog rolls in off the ocean, so the Sunset and Richmond stay gray while the Mission and East Bay stay sunny. September and October are the warm months.

fields.front: What happens to summer temperatures as you move inland, away from the Pacific?
fields.extra: The ocean is the Bay Area's air conditioner: on the same July day SF sits in the 60s, Berkeley the 70s, Walnut Creek the 90s. Why "through the tunnel" means bring shorts.

fields.front: Which earthquake fault runs directly under Berkeley and the East Bay hills?
fields.extra: It passes right through Cal's Memorial Stadium. Fault siblings: the San Andreas is the famous coastal one; the Hayward is the one under your feet.

fields.front: The San Andreas Fault runs along which side of the Bay Area?
fields.back: The western, coastal side, down the Peninsula.
fields.extra: Source of the 1906 San Francisco quake. In Berkeley the fault under your feet is the Hayward, not the San Andreas.

fields.front: Which big mountain rises east of the East Bay hills, over Contra Costa County?
fields.extra: 3,849 ft, the giant on the eastern horizon from any East Bay high point. Peak siblings: Diablo is east; Tamalpais is north, across the bay in Marin.

fields.front: Which peak dominates the Marin skyline, seen looking north across the bay?
fields.extra: The "sleeping lady" silhouette above the Golden Gate, and the birthplace of mountain biking. Peak siblings: Tam is north in Marin; Diablo is east in Contra Costa.
